name: neurram
display_name: NeuRRAM (130 nm RRAM, 48 cores of 256 x 256; wan2022a)

validity.array_size_assumed: 48 cores of 256 x 256 1T1R RRAM, a weight a differential pair of cells (wan2021edge p.2-3; wan2022a p.10); 4-bit output
validity.notes: MVM time and energy from one operating point of the Nature paper (Extended Data Table 1: 4-bit inputs, 4-bit weights, 6-bit outputs, wan2022a PDF p.28); write-verify parameters page-sourced (wan2022a Methods, PDF p.10), one cell written at a time; the write energy per pulse is a derived band (no write current or write energy is printed in the chip paper, its refs. 41 and 52 or its code release; the band rests on the paper's word-line capacitance and the release's gate biases, amplitude ceiling and verify voltage), per RRAM device, two devices holding a signed weight; the endurance is a device-class proxy (lee2011a, a TaOx bilayer RRAM cell), worn by 8.52 pulses per cell write.

e_mac.citation: wan2022a Extended Data Table 1, PDF p.28
e_mac.note: [U-C C-2] 'TOPS/W 43 | 40 | 16 | 7' at input bits 1 / 2 / 4 / 8, weight bits 4 and output bits 3 / 5 / 6 / 10 (read at 300 dpi, fetch intake constants_write_energy.md sec. 5): 16 TOPS/W at 4-bit inputs, the operating point of t_cycle; 1 MAC = 2 OPs, so 2 / 16e12 J = 125 fJ per MAC. gallo2022a Extended Data Table II repeats the 16 (the earlier, secondary reading).

t_cycle.citation: wan2022a Extended Data Table 1, PDF p.28
t_cycle.note: [U-C C-2] 'Latency of a 256x256 MVM (us) 1.4 | 1.6 | 3.9 | 10.7' at input bits 1 / 2 / 4 / 8: 3.9 us at the e_mac point (4-bit inputs, 4-bit weights, 6-bit outputs). Check: 65,536 x 2 / 16e12 J = 8.192 nJ per MVM x 3.9 us = 31.9e-15 J s against the printed 'Energy-delay-product (J s 10^-15) 4.2 | 5.3 | 32.0 | 215.9'. One MVM is one step of the value window. Replaces 2.1 us (wan2021edge p.17), a point the Nature table does not print.

write_verify_iterations.note: 'With such settings, 99% of the RRAM cells can be programmed to the acceptance range within the time-out limit. On average each cell requires 8.52 set/reset pulses.'

e_write_per_cell.citation: wan2022a Methods, PDF p.10 and p.14; NeuRRAM code release v1.0 (wan2022a ref. 47, Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.6558399, archive root weierwan-Neurram_48core-2ed5f8d) python/wupdate_control.py:79, :90, :371-413 and the deployment notebooks' end_voltage=4.0 and vset_wl 3.0 (CNN, MNIST, RBM) / 3.3 (LSTM)
e_write_per_cell.derivation: [U-C3, B3] One programming pulse into one RRAM device, a band between two named corners (fetch intake constants_write_energy_b3.md sec. 2.3). Word line: 'each of the 256 access transistors contributes about 1.5 fF to a WL; WL drivers combined contribute about 48 fF to each WL' (PDF p.14), so 256 x 1.5 fF + 48 fF = 432 fF, charged once per pulse at C V^2 (the paper's 'P = fCV2'; the code pulses the word line with every pulse, '# WL, BL and SL all get pulsed', wupdate_control.py:79). Cell: V^2 g t over a 1 us pulse ('we set the initial set pulse voltage to be 1.2 V and the reset pulse voltage to be 1.5 V, both with an increment of 0.1 V and pulse width of 1 μs', PDF p.10; the code's pulse_width=1e-6, wupdate_control.py:372) at a conductance between 'We used gmin = 1 μS for all the models, and gmax = 40 μS for CNNs' (PDF p.10). Low: the set word line at its 3.0 V gate bias (vset_wl=3.0), 432 fF x 3.0^2 = 3.888 pJ, plus the first set pulse at gmin (vset_start=1.2, wupdate_control.py:388), 1.2^2 x 1 uS x 1 us = 1.44 pJ: 3.888 + 1.44 = 5.328 pJ. High: the amplitude ceiling of every deployment call (end_voltage=4.0) across a 40 uS cell, 4.0^2 x 40 uS x 1 us = 640 pJ, plus the reset word line at its 5.0 V gate bias (vreset_wl=5.0, wupdate_control.py:90), 432 fF x 5.0^2 = 10.8 pJ: 10.8 + 640 = 650.8 pJ. Nominal at the band's log-space centre, sqrt(5.328 x 650.8) = 58.885 pJ (the arithmetic: final_units/uc3/probes/arith_uc3.out).
e_write_per_cell.note: [U-C3, B3] Readings, named: R1 the full pulse amplitude across the cell (the 1T1R selector lowers the cell voltage, so R1 over-states the cell term); R2 an ohmic cell at its conductance during the pulse; R3 one full word-line swing per pulse; R4 inter-wire capacitance excluded, which keeps the word-line term a floor. Not priced: BL and SL line charging (capacitance not stated), the off-chip DAC and ADC, the board. The high corner is a reading, not a bound: RRAM is super-linear at high field and the scheme lets a cell overshoot past its target. The row is per pulse into one RRAM device, and write_verify_iterations (8.52) counts pulses per device, so one device write prices (e_write_per_cell + e_verify_read_per_cell) x 8.52 = 45.7 / 508.5 / 5,681 pJ, which replaces the earlier cell-level 12.3 pJ to 1.32 nJ (constants_write_energy.md sec. 2.2). A signed weight is a differential pair of devices ('G[0::2, :] = (W>0) * W * scale' / 'G[1::2, :] = -((W<0) * W) * scale', python/nn_layers.py:33-37), and the neurram bundle declares it ([U-C4] core_fields cells_per_weight 2 with weight_cell_rows 2, B3 intake open item 4): a core holds 128 x 256 weights of the geometry's 256 x 256 devices, and a written weight is priced for both of its devices, 2 x 45.7 / 508.5 / 5,681 = 91.5 / 1,017 / 11,362 pJ and two write steps, each device worn by every write of its weight. Missing quantity for a published value: the selector's write current at 3.0 V (set) and 5.0 V (reset) gate bias, or a measured programming energy; neither is printed in the chip paper, refs. 41 (zhao2017investigation) and 52 (wu2018a), or the release. Paper and code differ in two places: the reset start is 1.5 V in the paper but 1.2 V (in range) or 2.5 V (zero target) in the code (wupdate_control.py:411, :389); the time-out is 30 set-reset polarity reversals in the paper but 50, 30 or 20 iterations in the code (iteration_limit). The paper governs write_verify_iterations; the code fixes the amplitude ceiling, the gate biases and the verify voltage, which the paper does not state.

e_verify_read_per_cell.citation: wan2022a Methods, PDF p.10; NeuRRAM code release v1.0 (Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.6558399) python/adc_control.py:142 and python/wupdate_control.py:224-225, :241-242
e_verify_read_per_cell.derivation: [U-C3, B3] One verify read of one RRAM device after each pulse. The code reads 'return (vread - vref) / currents_avg' (adc_control.py:142) after every pulse, with vread=1.1, vref=0.9 in every deployment call, so 0.2 V across the cell; 'A RRAM read takes 1–10 μs, depending on its conductance.' (PDF p.10), at 1 uS to 40 uS (gmin, gmax). V^2 g t: 0.2^2 x 1 uS x 1 us = 0.04 pJ, 0.2^2 x 40 uS x 10 us = 16 pJ, nominal at the log-space centre 0.8 pJ.
e_verify_read_per_cell.note: [U-C3, B3] The cell term only, a read being in the ohmic regime; the off-chip ADC and the line charging are not priced, as for e_write_per_cell, and one read per pulse is the integrated projection's (the board averages read_cycles=8, wupdate_control.py:198). Which read time goes with which conductance is not stated, so the corners pair the extremes.

t_write_per_unit.derivation: One write-verify iteration of one cell = one programming pulse ('both with an increment of 0.1 V and pulse width of 1 us') plus its verify read ('A RRAM read takes 1-10 us, depending on its conductance'), so 2 - 11 us; nominal from 'such write-verify will take on average 56 us per cell' over 8.52 pulses = 6.5728 us.
t_write_per_unit.note: Per cell, one cell at a time: 'In the weight-programming mode, individual RRAM cells are selected for read and write.' (the neurram bundle's write path).

endurance_cycles.note: [U-C C-1] A device-class proxy, so stated: 'demonstrated cycling endurance values of 10^11, 5x10^10 and 10^10 at 0.5x0.5 um2 cell sizes respectively' (Fig. 2c), measured on a Pt/Ta2O5-x/TaO2-x/Pt bilayer cell switched by binary 10 ns pulses, not on NeuRRAM's TiN/HfOx/TaOx/TiN 1T1R cell (HfOx switching, wan2022a Methods, PDF p.10), whose endurance neither NeuRRAM paper states. Cycles are set/reset cycles; one write wears pulses_per_write of them. Nominal at the band's log-space centre.

pulses_per_write.note: [U-C C-1] 'On average each cell requires 8.52 set/reset pulses.' Each set or reset pulse counts as one endurance cycle (owner decision B1, 2026-10-27), an upper reading of the wear, a full cycle being a set and a reset; the array iterations that re-program drifted cells ('We use 3 iterations in all our neural-network demonstrations', PDF p.10-11) are not counted, the drifted fraction being unstated.
